title: Impact of Inspiration Time in the Respiratory Cycle on Airway Mechanics and Homogeneity of Lung Ventilation in Premature Infants <34 weeks - a Pilot Study
summary: When ventilating premature babies, it is a common problem that individual sections of the lungs are not sufficiently ventilated, while other areas are over-inflated. This can lead to a ruptured lung, but also to chronic lung damage. We are investigating a possible strategy to ventilate the lungs more gently in such a situation. We and other units are already using similar strategies successfully, but there are no systematic studies on this. For this purpose, the premature infant is ventilated particularly quickly and, as part of the study, we simultaneously measure various parameters that help to assess the pressure load on the lungs and the homogeneity of lung ventilation.
conditions: Respiratory mechanics and homogeneity of lung ventilation

interventions.name: Long inspiratory times vs. short inspiratory times. Over a period of 12 minutes, different inspiratory times (0.1-0.4s) are set and the breathing mechanics are assessed via intratidal respiratory mechanics analysis and lung ventilation via EIT monitoring.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. gestational age < 34 weeks gestation
2. invasive ventilation
Exclusion criteria:
1. severe congenital pulmonary or cardiac malformations
2. chromosomal abnormalities
3. severe ventilatory instability
